query: Using the reported HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy as the starting material and its quasi-static properties—786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain—as the baseline, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to overcome limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure as strain rate increases under adiabatic dynamic deformation? Specify the intervention and mechanism, predict changes relative to the baseline in strength, uniform deformation, localization resistance, and impact-induced energy release, define the strain-rate and loading conditions over which the prediction applies, cite supporting evidence from the reported refractory-alloy literature, and describe a matched baseline-versus-intervention experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor tungsten content (e.g., 5–10 at.% W) to the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy will promote a stable dual‐phase microstructure that delays the onset of adiabatic shear localization under dynamic loading. This, in turn, will improve strain hardening and uniform deformation—mitigating poor uniform deformability and rapid failure at high strain rates.
generation.material_initial_state: HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy with quasi-static properties of 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain.
generation.intervention: Introduce minor tungsten additions (approximately 5–10 at.% substitution) into the alloy’s composition.
generation.conditions: Adiabatic dynamic compression testing at strain rates between 1000 and 3000 s⁻¹ at room temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a tungsten-stabilized dual-phase microstructure that increases phase stability and enhances dislocation interactions.
generation.mechanism: The presence of tungsten is anticipated to enhance dislocation pinning and promote the formation of a dual-phase structure, which together delay adiabatic shear band initiation. This mechanism mitigates rapid strain localization by counteracting local thermal softening effects at high strain rates, resulting in improved strain hardening and a more uniform deformation process.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy, the tungsten-modified alloy is predicted to exhibit an increase in dynamic yield strength by roughly 10–15%, enhanced uniform plastic deformation (with dynamic fracture strain potentially improving towards 17–20%), and a delayed onset of adiabatic shear localization, leading to a more distributed energy release under impact.
generation.baseline: HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy with quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and 13.5% fracture strain.
generation.boundary: This prediction is expected to hold under adiabatic dynamic conditions with strain rates between 1000 and 3000 s⁻¹ at room temperature. Outside these conditions or under non-adiabatic, cyclic, or thermal fatigue conditions, the effects remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements and the long-term stability of the tungsten-induced dual-phase microstructure require further investigation; effects under cyclic loading or varying temperatures are not predicted here.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one set of the baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy and another with a 5–10 at.% tungsten addition. Subject both sets to identical adiabatic dynamic compression tests at strain rates between 1000 and 3000 s⁻¹ at room temperature. Utilize high-speed imaging and digital image correlation to monitor the onset and progression of shear localization, as well as to quantify strain fields and deformation uniformity.
measurements: Time and strain at which adiabatic shear bands first form
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten-containing alloy does not exhibit statistically significant improvements over the baseline—specifically, if the dynamic yield strength does not increase by roughly 10–15%, if the dynamic fracture strain does not improve by at least 4–6 percentage points, or if there is no measurable delay or reduction in shear band formation under identical test conditions—the hypothesis is falsified.

Serrated steps observed in the stress–strain curve of W0 suggest a susceptibility to plastic instability. Under dynamic conditions, the yield strength of each alloy is significantly enhanced compared with the quasi-static conditions. This study demonstrates that the addition of W significantly enhances the mechanical properties of TiZrMo alloys, with the phase ratio effectively being controlled by adjusting the elemental composition. As a result, a dual-phase Ti40Zr40Mo10W10 HEA was successfully fabricated and subjected to comprehensive quasi-static and dynamic loading experiments to evaluate its energy release capability and mechanical properties for potential structural applications. The Ti40Zr40Mo10W10 HEA demonstrated exceptional quasi-static mechanical performance, with a yield strength of 1490 MPa, an ultimate strength of 2200 MPa, and a fracture strain of 30%. Under dynamic loading at a strain rate of 3000 s−1, the alloy exhibited an even higher ultimate strength of 2300 MPa and maintained a fracture strain of 24%, showcasing its remarkable ability to retain plasticity under extreme conditions. Additionally, the Ti40Zr40Mo10W10 HEA displayed significant chemical energy release and a high energy release capacity. reading.lever: Introduce minor tungsten additions to HfZrTiTa0.53 to promote a stable dual-phase microstructure and delay shear localization.
reading.why: Tungsten addition has proven to enhance dynamic ductility and strength in related HEAs, thereby potentially offsetting limited strain hardening and rapid failure under adiabatic conditions.
